proposals.hypothesis: Li2MgCl4 is a wide-gap, Li-rich chloride built from Mg2+, which is very hard to reduce. Chloride anions are chemically close to the Cl in Li6PS5Cl, so the contact with the sulfide electrolyte should avoid the S- and P-releasing reactions that gave the oxide and phosphate coatings their large penalties. The halide family has not yet been tested beyond LiF, so this is a chemically distinct probe. Its oxidative stability near 4 V vs Li is a risk to monitor.
proposals.motivation: Oxide and phosphate coatings (Li3PO4, Li2O, Li6Zr2O7, LiAlSiO4, Li3BO3) all showed contact penalties of about 0.2 eV/non-Li atom or more, driven by S/Cl-releasing reactions with the sulfide. Halide chemistry has not been tested except LiF, which was poor for other reasons.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating phosphate that is electrochemically stable up to about 4 V vs Li. It is chemically compatible with both the LiCoO2 cathode and the sulfide Li6PS5Cl electrolyte, and it is a well-studied protective coating for oxide cathodes in sulfide-based cells. It is a reasonable first candidate for a low interfacial penalty.

LiF is a wide-gap, electrochemically robust fluoride that is thermodynamically very stable against both LiCoO2 and the sulfide Li6PS5Cl. Its high oxidation stability should resist the 4 V cathode potential, and it is unlikely to drive reductive decomposition of the sulfide. It is a well-known protective coating and a plausible low-penalty contact compared with the Li3PO4 result, which had a sulfur/chlorine-releasing contact penalty of 0.34 eV per non-Li atom.
